_comment: Every scheduled job on this Mac, with how late it may run before the queue skips it.
maxLateMinutes is the honest question: if this fires now instead of at its cron time,
is the work still worth doing? A nightly sweep landing at 08:30 is noise, so it is
skipped. A Universal Credit check Mica needs is still worth sending at lunchtime, so it
is not. Sweeps get tight limits; anything that touches a person or an obligation gets a
generous one.
mode: 'wrapped' jobs are launchd shell commands run via job-queue.py run, so their PID
proves liveness. 'cooperative' jobs are Claude routines that call acquire and release
from their SKILL.md, where only the lease can free a crashed session.
Crons are standard five-field, LOCAL time, Sunday = 0.
queued:false means the job runs OUTSIDE the queue on purpose. Both such jobs exist to
report on or clean up after the others, so waiting behind a stuck routine would stop them
doing the one thing they are for. They are still listed here so the morning digest watches
needs: what must be true before the job may start. Five of the seven jobs that
failed every day were not broken. They fired the instant the Mac woke, before the
network and Google Drive were up, and reported a hard failure. The queue now waits
up to readyWaitMinutes (default 10) and DEFERS rather than failing if still not
ready. A drive probe READS A BYTE: an unmounted Drive folder still exists and still
lists, and only fails on open with 'Resource deadlock avoided'.
8 Aug 2026: the fourteen Claude routines were absorbed into one, `daily-ops`.
Serialising them behind a lock stopped them overwriting each other, then created a
worse failure: a routine suspended by the Mac sleeping keeps HOLDING the lock.
drift-monitor held it 4h54m while asleep, so everything behind it waited and was then
skipped for lateness. A lock cannot fix a machine that sleeps, because the lock sleeps
too. One routine running in sequence has nothing to overlap with and nothing to skip.
The lock now only guards the short shell jobs, and they heartbeat so a sleeping one
frees it in minutes.
them: a job left out of this file entirely is a job nobody notices has stopped.

mac-guard.note: reaps preview servers and test browsers that outlived their session. Must run even while a routine holds the queue, since a stuck routine is exactly when strays pile up

job-digest.note: reports on the queue, so it must never wait behind it

daily-ops.note: THE one Claude routine. Never skipped for lateness (maxLate 1440) — it IS the daily run, and skipping it means nothing happens at all. Unqueued: it runs for an hour or more and must not hold the lock the short shell jobs need.

daily-ops-guard.note: alarms if daily-ops left no phase-1 mark by 08:00 London — the scheduler stamped lastRunAt on 15 Aug 2026 while delivering the run to no session, so only the mark counts. Reports on the routine, so it must never wait behind anything. London gate lives in the code, not this cron (Mac timezone moves with Kevin).
